description.narrative: DKT is a non-profit private sector organization, is addressing challenges in SRHR through the private sector approach. Their program aims to improve access to SRHR information, commodities and services by social marketing, leveraging social media and forming partnerships with private sector clinics and pharmacies. DKT plans to enhance post abortion care services while challenging traditional norms and taboos to improve access to vital information. The organization will apply technology, including chatbots and hotline services run by trained counselors, to provide support related to abortion and long­ acting reversible contraceptive (LARC) aftercare. DKT will train private sector providers to increase prescriptions of LARC.

DKT är en ideell organisation inom den privata sektorn som arbetar med SRHR genom den privata sektorn. Deras program syftar till att förbättra tillgången till SRHR-information, varor och tjänster genom social marknadsföring, utnyttjande av sociala medier och partnerskap med kliniker och apotek inom den privata sektorn. DKT planerar att förbättra eftervården vid abort samtidigt som man utmanar traditionella normer och tabun för att förbättra tillgången till viktig SRHR information. Organisationen kommer att använda teknik, inklusive chatbots och hotline-tjänster som drivs av utbildade rådgivare, för att ge stöd i samband med eftervård vid abort och långverkande reversibla preventivmedel (LARC). DKT kommer att utbilda vårdgivare inom den privata sektorn för att öka förskrivningen av LARC.

Objective 1: Strengthened supply chain by increasing availability of modern contraceptive methods and safe (post) abortion Objective 2: Expanded access to SRH information and services Objective 3: Improved quality of sexual and reproductive health care through capacity building

description.narrative:
Ability to import commodities Import approvals remained tightly restricted throughout the year. In many cases, approved license amounts corresponded to only 23% of the requested value, creating significant uncertainty for supply planning and inventory management. To manage this, DKT maintained close and continuous follow-up to ensure that regulatory updates and announcements were not missed. At the same time, import license applications were submitted at levels higher than actual procurement needs in order to secure sufficient approved volumes aligned with the annual supply plan. DKT also adjusted shipment time lines, revised procurement priorities, and ensured the availability of high-demand products. A survey data for 2025 confirms that 97% of beneficiaries were able to effectively access and utilize the reproductive health solutions they required.
Capacity to self-finance through sales revenue In 2025, DKT Myanmar demonstrated strong resilience, achieving an annual CYP of 810,550. This represents a recovery to 95% of its annual target, compared to 55% in the previous year. This performance was achieved despite a challenging operating environment, including a mid-year transportation crisis and continued restrictions on import licenses. In 2025 the self financing was at 77%. The target had been put at 80%
Below results are from the handover conclusion of performance based on 2025 DKT annual report.
Health outcomes Significant results are also reflected in measurable health outcomes for 2025. DKT helped avert estimated more than 303,000 unintended pregnancies, representing a 31% increase compared to 2024, as well as 116,969 unsafe abortions. This highlights the continued high demand for reproductive health services in a fragile context. By translating operational resilience into tangible health impact, DKT also estimates to have prevented 150 maternal deaths and 641 child deaths, corresponding to improvements of 11% and 31% respectively compared to the previous year.
Digital outreach DKTs digital media presence across its key brands declined notably in terms of followers, growth, and engagement compared to the previous year. A significant share of sexual and reproductive health (SRH) content was flagged or removed due to platform community standards, often being categorised as prescription drugs or sexually suggestive or explicit content. These restrictions negatively affected reach, engagement, and audience growth, limiting the effectiveness of organic digital communication on SRH.
